content: Cognitive capacity should be evaluated regularly in individuals with diabetes, particularly in those who have documented cognitive impairments or in older adults who are at risk for cognitive decline. Cognitive functions, including attention, memory, logical reasoning, and problem-solving, are critical for effective self-management of diabetes. Cognitive decline is frequently observed in individuals with long-standing type 1 diabetes and can significantly impair their ability to adhere to self-care routines, manage medications, and maintain proper blood glucose control. Factors such as recurrent episodes of hypoglycemia, prolonged duration of diabetes, and vascular complications are known to increase the risk of cognitive dysfunction. For individuals experiencing cognitive decline, healthcare providers should modify diabetes management plans to address these changes. This may involve incorporating support from family members or caregivers to assist with self-care tasks and ensure effective diabetes management.
